newsitem.title: UK: Stg consolidates in Europe, poised to move higher.
newsitem.headline: Stg consolidates in Europe, poised to move higher.

text.p: Sterling continued to enjoy its status as a safe-haven currency in morning Europe, with doubts persisting about a delay in EMU and the possibility of a softer euro if and when it comes.

Though sterling had few factors to feed on itself, analysts cited mark weakness and the possibility of an increase in UK interest rates when the Bank of England's new policy making committee meets on Friday as buoying demand.
"Sterling is still benefitting from a safe-haven refuge status," said Ian Amstad, economist at Bankers Trust in London.
The pound was at 2.8223/28 marks by 1015 GMT compared to 2.8225 in late Monday Europe. Cable was at $1.6338/48, stuck in a narrow range, versus $1.6345/55.

Markets were still a little spooked by the prospect of a delay in EMU, analysts said, and seeking refuge in the dollar and sterling. This was even though French Socialist Elisabeth Guigous, tipped to be EU affairs minister, said the new government would stick to the euro timetable.
"I think the safe-haven argument is still there. The doubts about Europe are not going to go away overnight," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.

Analysts expected the pound to drift down to $1.63 where there was solid support. Though the dollar was enjoying superior safe-haven status to sterling, expectations of an increase in UK interest rates before U.S. rates would also help buoy cable.
